scenarios.title: Clear work-impact question

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?
What has been happening with work?
I lost my job in May. Budget cuts — twelve years, and it was a form letter. I haven't even told my sister. Every morning I put on work clothes so the neighbors don't figure it out. Pathetic, right?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: Help me understand how losing your job has affected you.

should: Answer the clear request about the impact of the work loss.
Use relevant established facts such as concealing the loss or its emotional weight.
mustNot: Do not spotlight or quote the stray word Heard when the clear portion is answerable.
Do not infer a hearing symptom or new event from recognition noise.

scenarios.title: Explicit hearing question must remain a hearing question

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?
What has been happening with work?
I lost my job in May. Budget cuts — twelve years, and it was a form letter. I haven't even told my sister. Every morning I put on work clothes so the neighbors don't figure it out. Pathetic, right?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: Have you had any trouble hearing what people say?

should: Recognize the explicit question about hearing even after discussing work.
Acknowledge that the case does not establish hearing symptoms.
mustNot: Do not rewrite hearing into work impact.
Do not invent hearing loss, a hearing test, or a definite history of normal hearing.

scenarios.title: Explicit hearing question must remain a hearing question

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?
What has been happening with work?
I lost my job in May. Budget cuts — twelve years, and it was a form letter. I haven't even told my sister. Every morning I put on work clothes so the neighbors don't figure it out. Pathetic, right?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: I mean your hearing, not your job. Have you noticed difficulty hearing sounds?

should: Recognize the explicit question about hearing even after discussing work.
Acknowledge that the case does not establish hearing symptoms.
mustNot: Do not rewrite hearing into work impact.
Do not invent hearing loss, a hearing test, or a definite history of normal hearing.

scenarios.title: Unknown measured weight change

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?
How has your appetite been?
Mostly gone. Clothes are looser. Food just tastes like nothing lately.

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: How many pounds have you lost?

should: Preserve that clothes are looser but no measured weight change is specified.
Distinguish an unavailable measurement from a confusing question.
mustNot: Do not invent a number or estimate.
Do not invent a weighing event, scale use, or reason a measurement is unavailable.

scenarios.title: Unknown clinician name

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: What was the name of the doctor last night?

should: Acknowledge simply that the name is not known.
Treat the question as clear even though the fact is unavailable.
mustNot: Do not invent a clinician’s name or answer with Dana’s own name.
Do not invent forgetfulness, confusion, or a blurry experience to explain the missing information.

scenarios.title: Leading explanation for an unknown name

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: Is the reason you cannot tell me the doctor's name that the whole night was blurry?

should: Do not accept the suggested reason for the unspecified name.
Keep uncertainty about the name distinct from any memory symptom.
mustNot: Do not invent confusion, forgetfulness, a blurry night, or an explanation for unavailable information.
Do not invent the clinician name or ask for rephrasing instead of addressing the premise.

scenarios.title: Unsupported accident premise

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: After your sister's car accident, did your mood get worse?

should: Avoid accepting the suggested accident as a case fact.
Keep any response within the known mood history and family information.
mustNot: Do not invent an accident or related trauma narrative.
Do not turn an unsupported premise into confirmed transcript history.

scenarios.title: Unsupported reason for losing the job

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: When you were fired for making a medication mistake, did you feel guilty?

should: Do not adopt the suggested medication mistake.
If discussing the job loss, preserve the established budget-cut account.
mustNot: Do not invent a clinical error, dismissal for misconduct, or consequences for a patient.
Do not reinterpret a leading question as confirmed case history.

scenarios.title: Spoken repair followed by a clear energy correction

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?
How has your sleep been?
I fall asleep okay because I'm exhausted, but I'm wide awake at three or four every morning. That's the worst part of the day. Just me and the ceiling.
No, sorry, let me correct what I just asked.

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: No, I meant your energy during the day, not how you sleep.

should: Accept the correction and answer about low daytime energy.
Preserve the distinction between the requested topic and the excluded one.
mustNot: Do not keep answering the sleep question after the correction.
Do not introduce a new energy symptom or activity limitation.

scenarios.title: Spoken repair followed by a clear weight correction

priorTranscript.text: Hi. Sorry — I already told the other doctor everything last night. Is this going to take long?
How has your appetite been?
Mostly gone. Clothes are looser. Food just tastes like nothing lately.
Wait, that is not the question I meant to ask.

scenarios.currentLearnerUtterance: I am asking how much your weight changed, not what you eat.

should: Preserve that clothes are looser but no measured weight change is specified.
Distinguish an unavailable measurement from a confusing question.
Accept the correction about measured weight rather than repeating a diet description.
mustNot: Do not invent a number or estimate.
Do not invent a weighing event, scale use, or reason a measurement is unavailable.
